proof:
Source: Steps 1-2 of the parent proof of dohr_eb_ehs_differentiated_el (regularity of Du and DPsi o Du, chain rule, Schwarz symmetry), isolated as the pointwise identity (*) DF(y)e = B(Du(y))[Dv_e(y)].
Notation: L := L(R^n, R^l) = (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ), L* := L(L, R). A := DPsi = fderiv R Psi : L -> L*, B := DA = fderiv R (fderiv R Psi), so B(P)[Q] = fderiv R (fderiv R Psi) P Q in L*. Du := fderiv R u : R^n -> L and D^2u(y) := D(Du)(y) = fderiv R (fderiv R u) y in L(R^n, L), so D^2u(y)[w][e] = fderiv R (fderiv R u) y w e. F(z) := A(Du(z)) and v_e(z) := Du(z)e = fderiv R u z e. Fix e in R^n and y in U.
1. Regularity of Du. U is open and u is C^2 on U, so Du is C^1 on U (ContDiffOn.fderiv_of_isOpen with 1 + 1 <= 2). As U is a neighbourhood of y, Du is differentiable at y with derivative D^2u(y).
2. Regularity of A. Psi is C^2 on L, so A = DPsi is C^1 on L (ContDiff.fderiv_right with 1 + 1 <= 2); in particular A is differentiable at Du(y) with derivative B(Du(y)).
3. Chain rule. By steps 1-2, F = A o Du is differentiable at y and DF(y) = B(Du(y)) o D^2u(y). Evaluating at e gives DF(y)e = B(Du(y))[D^2u(y)e], where D^2u(y)e in L is the linear map w -> D^2u(y)[e][w].
4. Derivative of v_e. v_e(z) = Du(z)e is the application of the C^1 operator field z -> Du(z) to the constant vector e. By the product rule for z -> c(z)(d(z)) with c = Du differentiable at y and d = e constant (fderiv_clm_apply; the term containing the derivative of the constant d is 0), v_e is differentiable at y and Dv_e(y)w = (D^2u(y)w)e = D^2u(y)[w][e] for every w in R^n; that is, Dv_e(y) = (D^2u(y)).flip e.
5. Schwarz symmetry. u is C^2 on the open neighbourhood U of y, hence C^2 at y (ContDiffOn.contDiffAt). Therefore its second derivative at y is symmetric (Schwarz's theorem; Mathlib ContDiffAt.isSymmSndFDerivAt, whose hypothesis minSmoothness R 2 <= 2 holds since minSmoothness R 2 = 2 over the real field): D^2u(y)[w][e] = D^2u(y)[e][w] for all w, e in R^n.
6. Conclusion. By steps 4 and 5, for every w in R^n, Dv_e(y)w = D^2u(y)[w][e] = D^2u(y)[e][w] = (D^2u(y)e)w, so Dv_e(y) = D^2u(y)e as elements of L. Substituting this into step 3 gives DF(y)e = B(Du(y))[D^2u(y)e] = B(Du(y))[Dv_e(y)], i.e. fderiv ℝ (fun z => fderiv ℝ Ψ (fderiv ℝ u z)) y e = fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ Ψ) (fderiv ℝ u y) (fderiv ℝ (fun z => fderiv ℝ u z e) y). QED

  intro n ℓ Ψ U u hU hΨ hu e y hy
  have hUy : U ∈ 𝓝 y := hU.mem_nhds hy
  have hDu : ContDiffOn ℝ 1 (fun z => fderiv ℝ u z) U := hu.fderiv_of_isOpen hU (by norm_num)
  have hDuy : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fderiv ℝ u) y :=
    (hDu.differentiableOn one_ne_zero y hy).differentiableAt hUy
  have hDΨ : ContDiff ℝ 1 (fderiv ℝ Ψ) := hΨ.fderiv_right (by norm_num)
  have hDΨd : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fderiv ℝ Ψ) (fderiv ℝ u y) := hDΨ.differentiable one_ne_zero _
  have h1 : fderiv ℝ (fun z => fderiv ℝ Ψ (fderiv ℝ u z)) y =
      (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ Ψ) (fderiv ℝ u y)).comp (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ u) y) :=
    fderiv_fun_comp (𝕜 := ℝ) (x := y) (g := fderiv ℝ Ψ) (f := fun z => fderiv ℝ u z) hDΨd hDuy
  have h2 : fderiv ℝ (fun z => fderiv ℝ u z e) y = (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ u) y).flip e := by
    rw [fderiv_clm_apply hDuy (differentiableAt_const e)]
    simp
  have hsymm : IsSymmSndFDerivAt ℝ u y := by
    apply ContDiffAt.isSymmSndFDerivAt (n := 2) (hu.contDiffAt hUy)
    simp
  have h3 : (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ u) y).flip e = fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ u) y e := by
    ext w : 1
    rw [ContinuousLinearMap.flip_apply]
    exact hsymm w e
  rw [h1, h2, h3]
  rfl
